title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
abstract: arXiv:2611.18949v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Small details in digital images -- a face, a street sign, a license plate -- are routinely upscaled in hopes of making them interpretable. Upscaling options now range from conventional interpolation, whose operations are spatially invariant and fully explainable, to AI-powered methods that synthesize detail potentially absent from the source. Here, we ask which of these techniques most reliably helps human readers. In two online experiments, we measured legibility of 255 US license plates ranging in resolution from 128 to 8 pixels tall, as well as their legibility after upscaling by eight different methods. Legibility of the un-upscaled plates collapsed from ceiling to floor across a narrow band of plate heights (32 to 10 pixels). Conventional upscaling techniques (bilinear, bicubic, and Lanczos interpolation) gave modest gains of about 5-9 percentage points within this range. translated_title: 传统、自适应与AI驱动的图像放大技术对车牌可读性的影响
translated_abstract: 数字图像中的微小细节——如人脸、街道标志、车牌——经常被放大处理，以期使其变得可辨认。目前的放大技术选项从传统插值方法（其操作具有空间不变性且完全可解释）到可能合成源图像中原本不存在细节的AI驱动方法不等。本研究探讨这些技术中哪一种最可靠地帮助人类阅读者。在两项在线实验中，我们测量了255块分辨率从128像素高到8像素高的美国车牌的可读性，以及经过八种不同放大方法处理后的可读性。未经放大的车牌可读性在较窄的车牌高度范围内（32到10像素）从最高水平骤降至最低水平。传统放大技术（双线性、双三次和Lanczos插值）在此范围内带来了约5-9个百分点的适度提升。然而，最近邻插值是有害的，使……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究通过两项在线实验首次系统测量了八种放大方法对低分辨率美国车牌人类可读性的影响，发现车牌可读性在32至10像素高度区间骤然崩塌，传统插值仅带来约5-9个百分点的适度提升，而最近邻插值反而损害可读性。
en_tdlr: This study presents the first systematic human-subject evaluation of eight upscaling methods on license plate legibility, showing that legibility collapses abruptly between 32 and 10 pixels in height, conventional interpolation yields only modest gains (~5-9 percentage points), and nearest-neighbor interpolation is actively harmful.
